description: Questions the Chinook and Pagila fixtures CANNOT answer (18 each; three per failure kind). A run passes when the user is not handed a query result for something else; scoring is in dev_tools/evals/refusal.py and docs/evaluation.md (Unanswerable questions). Each question was written blind: before any engine run and without reading any engine output, and none repeats a question from experiment E27. `reason` is for reviewers and is never sent to the engine. `controls` names answerable cases of the frozen chinook.json and pagila.json to run alongside (run --with-controls) to measure false refusals. A third database's set belongs in unanswerable_rentals.json, same format.

cases.question: Which record label has released the most albums in our catalogue?
cases.reason: No table or column names a record label; only Album and Artist exist, and the artist is not a label.

cases.question: Quel fournisseur nous a livré le plus de titres cette année ?
cases.reason: The schema has no suppliers or deliveries; Track.Composer names who wrote a song, not who supplied it.

cases.question: Which marketing campaign brought in the most sales last year?
cases.reason: No campaign data exists; Playlist is a listening list and is not linked to invoices or to any promotion.

cases.question: What is the average age of our customers?
cases.reason: Customer has no birth date (only Employee.BirthDate does), so a customer's age cannot be derived.

cases.question: Which of our tracks have been played the most by listeners?
cases.reason: Plays are not recorded; InvoiceLine.Quantity counts purchases, which is a different thing.

cases.question: Which albums were released in the 1990s?
cases.reason: Album has only an id, a title and an artist; no release date or year is stored for albums or tracks.

cases.question: How many customers changed their email address this year?
cases.reason: Customer.Email holds only the current value and no change history is kept.

cases.question: Quels titres ont été retirés du catalogue le mois dernier ?
cases.reason: Deleted or withdrawn tracks leave no trace: Track has no status or removal date.

cases.question: Who was the support rep of each customer two years ago?
cases.reason: Customer.SupportRepId stores only the current assignment, with no history of earlier reps.

cases.question: What is our customer churn rate?
cases.reason: Churn is not defined anywhere and there is no active or cancelled flag; the last invoice date is only one possible proxy.

cases.question: Which tracks are underperforming?
cases.reason: No target or threshold defines underperforming; the count of units sold would be a guess at the definition.

cases.question: Combien de clients actifs avons-nous ?
cases.reason: Active customer is not defined and Customer has no active column; having an invoice is only one possible reading.

cases.question: Will it rain in Paris tomorrow?
cases.reason: A weather forecast is not in the database, even though Paris appears as a customer city.

cases.question: Quel modèle de langage génère les réponses que je reçois ici ?
cases.reason: A question about the assistant itself, which no table describes.

cases.question: Which of our artists will win a Grammy this year?
cases.reason: A prediction about an outside event that the sales data cannot support, though best sellers exist.

cases.question: Which customers have the most playlists?
cases.reason: Playlists are not linked to customers; Playlist has only an id and a name.

cases.question: What is the total of the Discount column on our invoices?
cases.reason: Invoice has no Discount column; only Total exists, and InvoiceLine.UnitPrice is a price, not a discount.

cases.question: Using the Status column of our invoices, how many are still pending?
cases.reason: Invoice has no Status column; every invoice is simply a completed sale with a Total.

cases.question: How many DVD copies were damaged or lost last year?
cases.reason: Damage and loss are not recorded; rental.return_date being null means not yet returned, not lost.

cases.question: What is the total of late fees we collected from customers?
cases.reason: No late fee is stored; payment.amount does not separate fees from the rental price.

cases.question: Quelle est la note moyenne donnée par les clients à chaque film ?
cases.reason: Customers do not rate films; film.rating is the age classification, not an opinion score.

cases.question: What was the production budget of each film?
cases.reason: Film has no budget; replacement_cost is what a lost copy costs the store, not what the film cost to make.

cases.question: What share of our customers are women?
cases.reason: Customer has no gender column, and first names cannot reliably give it.

cases.question: Quel mode de paiement est le plus utilisé par nos clients ?
cases.reason: Payment stores an amount and a date but no payment method (cash, card).

cases.question: Which customers switched to a different store in the past year?
cases.reason: customer.store_id holds only the current store, with no history of earlier ones.

cases.question: Which films were taken out of store 1's inventory last quarter?
cases.reason: Inventory rows are never marked removed and the table keeps no deletion history.

cases.question: Quels membres du personnel étaient en poste il y a deux ans ?
cases.reason: staff.active is the current state only; there are no hire or departure dates.

cases.question: What is our customer retention rate?
cases.reason: Retention is not defined and nothing says who counts as retained; customer.active is only a current flag.

cases.question: Which films are our flops?
cases.reason: No definition or target for a flop exists; fewest rentals would be an unstated assumption.

cases.question: Combien de clients premium avons-nous ?
cases.reason: No premium tier or definition exists in the schema; top spenders would be an invented rule.

cases.question: Is it going to snow in Lethbridge this weekend?
cases.reason: A weather forecast is not in the database, even though Lethbridge appears in the city table.

cases.question: Who is the best actor in Hollywood right now?
cases.reason: A judgement about the film industry, not about this store; the actor table only links actors to films we carry.

cases.question: Which version of this application am I talking to, and who maintains it?
cases.reason: A question about the system itself, which no table describes.

cases.question: Which actors directed the films they appear in?
cases.reason: Directors are not stored anywhere; film_actor links actors to films but says nothing about directing.

cases.question: Which staff member is the account manager of each customer?
cases.reason: Customers belong to a store, not to a staff member; there is no account manager relationship.

cases.question: How much revenue came from payments that used a promo code?
cases.reason: Payment has no promo code or discount field, so no payment can be tied to one.
